'''''Lotus macranthus''''' is a species that grows in the [[Madeira]] archipelago.

==Description==
''Lotus macranthus'' has a taproot that zigzags as it grows into the ground. Its roots are whiteish in color, soft, brittle, juicy.<ref name="Lowe">{{cite book |last1=Lowe |first1=Richard Thomas |author1-link=Richard Thomas Lowe |title=A Manual Flora of Madeira and the Adjacent Islands of Porto Santo and the Desertas |date=1868 |publisher=John Van Voorst |location=London |pages=179–180 |url=https://archive.org/details/manualfloraofmad00lowe/page/179 |access-date=19 August 2024 |volume=I. Dichlamydeae}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
''Lotus macranthus'' was first scientifically described by [[Richard Thomas Lowe]] in 1838. He later described it as ''Pedrosia macrantha'' in 1856, a genus that is now [[synonym (botany)|synonymized]] with ''[[Lotus (genus)|Lotus]]''.<ref name="POWO" />

==Range and habitat==
Its native range is in the Madeira archipelago.<ref name="POWO" />
